statement: Let p = m + 3 and Q = B m+2 × [−1, 1], u = (v, b). Identify opposite points of ∂Q, and denote the quotient map by q : Q −→ RPp . There is a flat-continuous map Φ : RPp −→ Z0 m(Sm+1 ; Z2) with the following properties. (i) The map Φ is detecting in the sense of Definition 4.2, has no concentration of mass, and satisfies Φ(q(0, 0)) = ∂[Ω], M(Φ(q(0, 0))) = |Σ|, where Ω is the side of Σ opposite to N. For r = √ 1 − b2 its masses obey M(Φ(q(v, b))) ≤ { rm|Σ|, |v| < 1, rmσm, |v| = 1. (5.1) In particular |Σ| ≥ γm > σm, where γm is the constant in Lemma 4.4. (ii) The central parameter is the unique maximum, in the uniform sense that for every neigh- borhood U of (0, 0) in Q, sup u∈Q\U M(Φ(q(u))) < |Σ|. (5.2) (iii) Near (0, 0) these cycles are precisely the multiplicity-one boundaries of a smooth family of domains, with embedded boundaries parametrized by Σ. The normal derivative at the center, in the parameter direction (d, t) ∈ Rm+2 × R, is wd,t(x) = t + ⟨d, x⟩. (5.3) These variations form a p-dimensional subspace on which the area second variation is negative definite. 17 (iv) If ind(Σ) > p, there is a flat homotopy of Φ, supported in the image of a neighborhood of (0, 0), to a detecting map ~ Φ with no concentration of mass and sup ξ∈RPp M(~ Φ(ξ)) < |Σ|.
